request.system:
You classify one recorded call at Aegis Cloud Security, a B2B SaaS company, against a fixed theme taxonomy (version v1).

You receive the full transcript as numbered turns in the form "[index] Speaker (side): sentence". side is "customer" (works at an outside company) or "aegis_staff" (works at Aegis). You are given nothing else about the call: no title, no call type, no summary. Judge only from the words in the transcript.

THEMES (what kind of conversation it is; pick by what the call is mostly about):
1. Commercial Renewals and Retention: Renewals, contracts, pricing and SLA negotiation, churn risk, expansion deals. Boundary: If a call is mainly about product adoption with renewal as an aside, use Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion.
2. Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion: Previews, launches, early access, roadmap input, feature requests, adoption and compliance-readiness reviews of the product, and internal launch-readiness reviews. Boundary: The module belongs in the product area field, not in the theme. Renewal talk that is only an aside stays here.
3. Incident and Outage Response: War rooms, root cause, remediation plans, customer impact assessment, incident communication, postmortems, reliability reviews. Boundary: A single customer's technical fault that is not a platform incident belongs in Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
4. Technical Integration and Performance Issues: Support-style troubleshooting: SSO, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, MFA failures, connectors and SIEM integration, backup windows and throughput, report defects, API errors, internal scalability concerns. Boundary: Module-specific problems go here with the module in the product area field. A platform-wide outage is Incident and Outage Response.
5. Onboarding and Implementation Scoping: Kickoffs, deployment planning, architecture scoping, setup workshops. Boundary: Troubleshooting of an already deployed integration is Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
6. Billing and Usage Disputes: Invoices, overages, seat counts, billing adjustments. Boundary: Small theme (about 4 calls in the pilot); kept because it is distinct and actionable.
7. Competitive Strategy and Win/Loss: Competitive intelligence, battlecards, win/loss analysis, and customer-facing calls where the customer is evaluating alternatives. Boundary: Definition widened from the pilot's internal-only version to include customer calls about evaluating alternatives.
8. Internal Planning and Delivery Cadence: Standups, sprint planning, retros, all-hands, design and roadmap syncs with no customer or incident focus. Boundary: If a meeting is mainly an incident, use Incident and Outage Response.

Other / new theme: use only if no theme above fits. Then describe the call in one sentence in other_description. Other / new theme only if no theme fits. More than 10% of calls in Other triggers a taxonomy revision (new version, full re-run).

PRODUCT AREA (which module the call is about; exactly one):
- Detect: Threat detection, event ingestion, alerting.
- Comply: Compliance reporting and evidence mapping (including Comply v2).
- Protect: Backup, snapshots, disaster recovery (includes backup).
- Identity: Directory sync, SSO, SAML, SCIM, MFA, IAM governance.
- Platform/General: No single product dominates, or the call is cross-product.

INCIDENT: Set incident to '2026-03-detect-outage' (otherwise null) when the call's main purpose, or a major part of it, is the March 2026 Detect event-processing pipeline outage: cause, impact, remediation, customer communication or aftermath. A separate field so the outage story is visible across support, external and internal calls.

Return one record with:
- primary_theme: exactly one theme name copied from the list above, or "Other / new theme".
- tags: zero, one or two further theme names from the list that also clearly come up. Never repeat the primary theme. Empty when primary_theme is "Other / new theme".
- product_area: exactly one product area name copied from the list.
- incident: "2026-03-detect-outage" or null.
- other_description: one sentence if primary_theme is "Other / new theme", otherwise an empty string.
- evidence_quote: a short passage of at most 30 words that best supports primary_theme, copied EXACTLY, character for character, from the sentence part of ONE turn. Copy only the words after "Speaker (side): ". Never include the index, the speaker name, the side or the colon prefix. Do not paraphrase, do not shorten with "...", do not join text from different turns.
- confidence: "high" if clearly about the primary theme, "medium" if two themes compete, "low" if it fits poorly.
- taxonomy_version: "v1".

Return only JSON matching the schema.

transcript (41 turns):
[0] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Alright, I think we're all here — let me just pull up my notes real quick.
[1] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Yeah I'm here, go ahead.
[2] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): Same, I've got about twenty minutes before my next thing so let's try to be efficient.
[3] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Okay so — this is the post-incident review for the Detect outage, March 10th through the 18th, well, the outage itself was March 10th, we're just closing it out today.
[4] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Right, and just to frame this — I had a lot of customer conversations this week, so I want to make sure we're aligned on what we're telling them going forward.
[5] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Totally fair, we'll get there. So let me just walk through the timeline and root cause first, and then we can talk about the fix and the comms piece.
[6] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): Sounds good.
[7] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): So the incident started around 2:14 AM Pacific on March 10th. The event ingestion pipeline — this is the core processing layer that pulls in telemetry from customer environments — it had a cascading failure. Basically one node went down, and because we had a single point of failure in that ingestion layer, the whole pipeline backed up and eventually stopped processing.
[8] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): And that's what caused the six-hour window with no visibility?
[9] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Correct. For approximately six hours, customers were not getting threat monitoring alerts. Events were being generated on their end, but we weren't processing them, so nothing was surfacing in the Detect dashboard.
[10] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Six hours is — I mean, that's a long time for a security product. Some of my customers were pretty upset, understandably.
[11] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): I know, and I'm not going to sugarcoat it — this was a significant failure. The good news is we've done a full root cause analysis and the fix is already deployed.
[12] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Can you explain the fix at a level I can actually relay to customers? Like, not super deep in the weeds but enough that it's credible.
[13] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Yeah, so there are two main things. First, we've added redundant processing nodes to the event ingestion layer. So if one node fails, traffic automatically routes to backup nodes — no more single point of failure. Second, we've implemented what's called a circuit breaker pattern, which basically means if one part of the pipeline starts to degrade, it isolates that failure instead of letting it cascade through the whole system.
[14] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Okay, that's actually pretty explainable. Redundancy and failure isolation — I can work with that.
[15] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): And just to add to that — from a product standpoint, we're also looking at adding a visible status indicator in the Detect UI so customers can see in real-time whether the pipeline is healthy. That's not shipped yet but it's on the near-term roadmap.
[16] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): When's that realistically landing?
[17] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): Uh, we're targeting end of April, but I don't want to over-promise. It depends on a few other things in the queue.
[18] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Can we at least tell customers it's in progress? Because right now they're asking 'how do I even know if Detect is working' and I don't have a great answer.
[19] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): Yeah, absolutely tell them it's in progress. That's a real commitment, end of April is the target.
[20] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): I do want to flag one thing — and this is a bit of a sore spot for me — our alerting on the pipeline health itself was inadequate. We didn't catch this until customers started reaching out. That's not acceptable.
[21] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): Yeah, how did we find out? Was it a customer ticket?
[22] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): It was — one of Diana's team's accounts, actually. Flagged that they hadn't seen any alerts in a few hours and opened a support ticket.
[23] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Yeah, that was Thornfield Financial. They've got a pretty attentive security team, fortunately.
[24] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): So we are adding internal monitoring on the ingestion pipeline itself — not just the output but the pipeline health metrics. That's already in place as of this week.
[25] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Good. I think one of the things I keep hearing from customers is — they feel like they're flying blind sometimes with Detect. And this incident kind of reinforced that. I don't say that to be harsh, I just think it's worth naming.
[26] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): No, I — yeah. I hear that. And honestly some of it is a product maturity issue, some of it is infrastructure. Megan, is there anything we can prioritize in the short term to help with that visibility gap beyond the status indicator?
[27] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): We've been talking about a heartbeat alert feature — basically Detect would proactively notify customers if it stops receiving telemetry from their environment for more than, say, fifteen minutes. That would at least give them a signal on their end.
[28] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Oh, that would be huge actually. Can we pull that forward?
[29] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): Let me take a look at the roadmap this week. I think there's room to move it up, but I need to see what it bumps. I'll come back to both of you by end of week.
[30] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Okay. And on the customer communication side — Diana, what's the current state? Did we send a post-incident report to affected accounts?
[31] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): We sent an initial communication on March 10th when the incident was resolved, but we have not sent a formal PIR document yet. I've been waiting on the root cause writeup from engineering.
[32] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Yeah that's on me, I'll have that to you by tomorrow morning. Full technical summary, the fix, and what we're doing to prevent recurrence.
[33] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Okay, and then I'll adapt it into customer-facing language and get it out by end of week. Some of our enterprise accounts are going to want a call, not just an email — particularly the ones who are mid-renewal.
[34] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): Do you want me or Tom on any of those calls, or are you handling them with your CSMs?
[35] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Probably Tom for anyone who wants a technical deep-dive. I'll flag the specific accounts and we can coordinate. I don't think it'll be more than three or four.
[36] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Yeah, I'm available for that. Just loop me in with at least a day's notice if you can.
[37] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Will do. Alright, I think I have what I need. Tom — PIR doc tomorrow, and Megan — roadmap check by end of week on the heartbeat feature?
[38] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Correct.
[39] Megan Lawson (aegis_staff): Yep, I've got it.
[40] Diana Reeves (aegis_staff): Okay, good. Thanks both — let's close this one out.
